clue.text: Main division of the British Isles

definitions.text: Main division of the British Isles

parts.words: Main division of the British Isles
parts.note: the main is the open sea, so this is the stretch of sea dividing Britain from Ireland, not a political region

explanation.definitionFit: This body of water lies between Great Britain and Ireland, separating the two largest islands of the group.

clue.text: Tiddly earls taking one king out for traditional drink

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Tiddly earls taking one king out for traditional drink (4,3)': no reading of 'earls taking one king out' gives the letters of REAL ALE (EARLS plus A leaves an S and lacks E, L), so a word appears misprinted or missing and searches found no other text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Tiddly earls taking one king out for traditional drink

clue.text: Fix old-fashioned drawing instrument

parts.note: to fix something in place is to set it
a square is a stuffy, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: Someone repairs an antique piece of draughtsman's equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-angled triangular tool used by draughtsmen for drawing perpendicular lines.

clue.text: Carriage for one of the county set

definitions.meaning: a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of the nineteenth century
an English county south of London, one of the set of counties

explanation.surface: A carriage meant for a member of the horsey upper-class county set.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'county set' is the British landed gentry of the shires; here the phrase is read literally as the set of counties. SURREY is a county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same word: a horse-drawn passenger vehicle, and a home county bordering London.

clue.text: Reverence for old part of tree

definitions.text: Reverence for old part of tree

parts.words: Reverence for old part of tree
parts.note: the old part of a family tree is the earlier generations, and reverence for them is a religious practice

explanation.definitionFit: Veneration of deceased forebears, a practice found in many religions and cultures.

clue.text: River in East, with lots of people around

indicators.note: the group of people stands around the compass point, so one goes round the other

parts.note: gangs are groups of people

explanation.surface: A river in the Orient, with crowds gathered on its banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The great sacred waterway of northern India flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Valuable source yielding old minerals to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rich supply of something produces ancient ores in part.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a plentiful source of something profitable or useful, like a productive seam.

clue.text: Enterprising leader of Indian state

parts.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Describing the dynamic chief minister of a state in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'leader of Indian state', HEAD of GOA, but the charade puts the state first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambitious and keen to try new things is the adjectival sense of this hyphenated word.

clue.text: Serious measure for the army, but not the fleet

definitions.text: Serious measure for the army, but not the fleet

parts.words: Serious measure for the army, but not the fleet
parts.note: a measure is a dance step or tempo; a solemn one is used by soldiers on parade but sailors at sea do not walk in step

explanation.definitionFit: A solemn ceremonial military pace used at funerals and parades.

clue.text: Female player's Scottish manager

parts.note: an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: An actress's agent who comes from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland a FACTOR is the steward who manages a landed estate for its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish usage, this is the agent or steward managing property on behalf of a landowner.

clue.text: American flag a party adopted for state

parts.note: a regiment's flag is its colours, spelt colors in American English
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A political party takes up the Stars and Stripes as its banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted' simply links the pieces; 'American' signals the US spelling without a U.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Rocky Mountains, with Denver as its capital.

clue.text: Makes son a nobleman

parts.note: makes are brands of car, also called marques

explanation.surface: A father's action ennobles his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' looks like a verb but is a plural noun: brands of manufactured goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer ranking above an earl and below a duke in the British nobility.

clue.text: Hermitage, for example, in practice needing quiet setting

indicators.note: the quiet word forms a setting round the other, as a mount holds a jewel

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
use is practice or custom

explanation.surface: A hermit's retreat, where silent habits are required.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hermitage is the great art gallery in St Petersburg, not a hermit's cell.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hermitage in St Petersburg is a famous example of a public gallery of art and antiquities.

clue.text: Artist succeeded with mature ret-respective

indicators.note: retrospective, looking back, so the word for mature is read from end to start

parts.note: aged means mature
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A painter does well with a mature retrospective exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ret-respective' is retrospective printed with a stray hyphen, and it signals reading backwards; the art-world sense of a retrospective, a career exhibition, is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter famous for ballet dancers.

clue.text: Existing thinker?

parts.note: the philosopher whose famous dictum ties thinking to existing: I think, therefore I am

explanation.definitionFit: The French philosopher whose cogito argued his existence from the fact of his thinking.

clue.text: Feather-bedded person enjoys this in Australia

definitions.meaning: someone in a feather bed lies beneath the soft feathers of the quilt
the colloquial phrase for being in Australia or New Zealand, at the bottom of the globe

explanation.surface: Someone tucked up under the duvet in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Down is the soft feathers of a duvet; feather-bedded also suggests a pampered person.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean location is called this informally, Australia lying beneath Britain on a map, and a sleeper lies beneath the eiderdown.

clue.text: State advanced on country across its southern border

parts.note: new means modern or advanced
the country lying across the border to the south of this US state

explanation.surface: A state moves forward against the nation beyond its southern frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Southwest, bordering the nation it is named after.

clue.text: Person protesting in article, getting nothing right

parts.note: an object is an article or thing
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A demonstrator writing a newspaper piece gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a newspaper piece or a/the in grammar; here it is a physical thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who raises a protest or formal opposition, as a conscientious one does.

clue.text: Top-class flier in American sporting event

parts.note: superb means excellent, top-class
an owl is a bird, a flier

explanation.surface: An excellent bird appears at a US sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious split of the answer into two words is not the one the wordplay uses: the flier is a bird of prey that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual championship game of American football.

clue.text: Meat dish that shouldn't be swallowed

definitions.meaning: a pastry case filled with pork, eaten cold
rhyming slang for a lie, which one should not believe

explanation.surface: A savoury pie one is warned not to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: PORK PIE is British rhyming slang for a lie (often shortened to porky); to swallow a story is to believe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a cold British pastry with pork filling and, in rhyming slang, a falsehood.

clue.text: Covered by water, area was hard to find

indicators.note: to find says the answer is there in the clue's words, waiting to be found in them

explanation.surface: A flooded region was difficult to locate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is at the front; the letters sit inside 'area was hard', running across all three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded or swamped, with water washing over the surface.

clue.text: Initial course to study very little

parts.note: soup is often the first course of a meal
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A student takes a beginner's course without doing much.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount or trace, from French, as in a hint of garlic.

clue.text: Operatic hero's singular spirit

parts.note: one means single or singular
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: An opera's leading man has a unique soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene, the title character of Tchaikovsky's opera from Pushkin's verse novel.

clue.text: Show up a split involving right

indicators.note: the word for split involves, or takes in, the abbreviation

parts.note: to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Expose a rift involving the political Right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show up' looks like expose, but it means turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or reach a destination, synonyms for turning up.

clue.text: Competitor one has beaten

parts.note: the contestant the winner has just beaten, finishing in second place

explanation.definitionFit: The contestant finishing second, beaten only by the winner.

clue.text: Improve on record mark? Excellent

parts.note: to top a record is to beat it
a notch is a mark or nick

explanation.surface: Beating a previous best by a mark is outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Sudden malfunction producing extremely general irritation

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word, its first and last letters, are used

parts.note: an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: A breakdown causing widespread annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief unexpected fault in a machine or system.

clue.text: Run through what's comparatively oblique

definitions.meaning: to pierce with a spit or blade
more skew, the comparative of skew meaning slanting

explanation.surface: Something more slanting pierces a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a pointed rod to pierce food and, read as a comparative, more slanted.

clue.text: Locate exactly where angels were supposed to dance?

definitions.text: where angels were supposed to dance?
definitions.meaning: medieval scholars supposedly debated how many angels could dance on the head of a pin

explanation.surface: Finding precisely the spot for the angels' dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverbial scholastic question asked how many angels could dance on the point of a pin.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify a location precisely, as with the tip of a needle.
